title: Prioritization Stitchboard — Sprint 28 Notes
content:
Purpose:
- Rapidly align the console/product team on which console/tooling tickets to carry into Sprint 28. This is a working doc (stitchboard) — intentionally fragmentary.

Desired outcomes for Sprint 28 (vote-based):
1) Ship a low-friction route for per-route latency budgets in the Console (MVP UI + backend flag).
2) Reduce intake queue by 20% via better triage prompts and an automated routing rule for infra-related bugs.
3) Prototype a compact wireframe for ‘Model Variant Rollouts’ inside the Rollouts page (click-through demo).

Context / Background:
- Several folks escalated that teams are pinged for latency regressions with no clear SLO mapping. Product wants a first-pass UI for route-level budgets that ties to existing route configs.
- Intake queue backlog: ~120 items, ~40 flagged infra/ops items that engineering sorts through during grooming. We can reduce cycle time by moving simple rules into intake automation.
- ‘Model Variant Rollouts’ is higher-effort but strategic — we want a clickable prototype to validate UX before committing Dedicated resources.

Intake summary (high-impact candidates):
A. ROUTE-BUDGETS (JIRA-1024) — UI + API for per-route latency budget.
  - Effort: small-medium (UI work, wireframe -> frontend + backend flag).
  - Benefit: high for customers using dedicated/hosted SLAs.
  - Key unknowns: mapping to existing SLO data pipeline; telemetry tag availability.
  - Wireframe notes: small inline editor on Route > Settings: threshold slider (p50/p95), reason field, save as policy. Quick confirm modal.

B. INTAKE-AUTOFILTER (JIRA-1102) — automated routing for infra-related reports.
  - Effort: small (rules + matchers in intake service).
  - Benefit: medium (reduces engineering triage time).
  - Wireframe notes: admin UI to define rules (contains simple predicates: title contains, label matches). Start with templated rules: "cloud-provider error" -> route to infra.

C. VARIANT-ROLLOUT-PROTOTYPE (design spike) — click-through wireframe + acceptance checklist.
  - Effort: medium-high (design + PM + small front-end prototype).
  - Benefit: strategic (enables safe rollouts and A/B testing of models).
  - Scope for sprint: prototype only, no backend persistence.

Prioritization criteria used (explicit):
- Customer pain (urgent escalations) = weight 4
- Implementation speed (time-to-MVP) = weight 3
- Cross-team dependencies = weight 2
- Long-term strategic value = weight 3

Quick scoring (1-5) summary from workshop:
- ROUTE-BUDGETS: pain=4, speed=3, deps=2, strategic=3 => weighted ~ (16+9+4+9)=38
- INTAKE-AUTOFILTER: pain=3, speed=5, deps=1, strategic=2 => weighted ~ (12+15+2+6)=35
- VARIANT-ROLLOUT-PROTOTYPE: pain=2, speed=2, deps=3, strategic=5 => weighted ~ (8+6+6+15)=35

Decision proposal (MVP Sprint 28 slice):
- Primary sprint focus: ROUTE-BUDGETS (A) as the main deliverable.
- Secondary parallel work: INTAKE-AUTOFILTER (B) as a low-effort paired task (aim to ship small rule set).
- Defer VARIANT-ROLLOUT-PROTOTYPE (C) to a design sprint mid-sprint if bandwidth remains; otherwise schedule as dedicated spike in Sprint 29.

Sprint scope and acceptance criteria (draft):
1) ROUTE-BUDGETS (owner: Maya):
  - UI: Route Settings panel contains new "Latency Budget" section with slider and p95/p50 toggle.
  - API: Console calls a feature-flagged backend endpoint to persist budget (no telemetry enforcement in Sprint 28).
  - Acceptance: create budget, load existing budgets, edit and save, modal confirmation, unit tests for frontend form validation, smoke test flow passes on staging.

2) INTAKE-AUTOFILTER (owner: Priya):
  - UI: Admin -> Intake Rules shows list, can enable/disable template rule, basic text predicate editor.
  - Backend: simple matcher service uses title/body regex and label heuristics, routes matching items to infra queue.
  - Acceptance: ship 3 templated rules, metric: infra-assigned intake items down 30% in first 48h.

3) VARIANT-ROLLOUT-PROTOTYPE (owner: Evan):
  - Deliverable: Figma click-through showing create-rollout flow, select model variant(s), percentage controls, rollback CTA.
  - Acceptance: internal walkthrough with at least two engineers + PM, sign-off to convert to implementation ticket.

Wireframe / UX granular notes (rough):
- Route Budgets UI: keep it minimal — prefer inline inline-edit vs modal-heavy. Add a subtle link "What budget means" so UX can explain enforcement vs alerting.
- Budget naming: allow optional label; display next to route name in list as pill 'Budget: 120ms p95'.
- Accessibility: slider must be keyboard accessible; add text input for ms value.
- Intake rules editor: start with pattern presets and a "test against sample" box so admins can paste a title and see match result.
- Rollouts prototype: prioritize visual clarity for traffic split; use an animated percentage dial to convey flow.

Open questions / Risks (not exhaustive):
- Telemetry: can we expose p95 calculation per-route within backend slices without a major infra change? (ENG infra to confirm)
- Backwards compatibility: existing route export/import may break if budgets are added — need schema migration plan.
- Adoption: will teams prefer budgets or rely on alerts? We should ship a small survey in-app after GA.

Dependencies & owners:
- Metrics infra (ask: can add route-level p95 tag) -> Owner: SRE (TBD ticket).
- Intake service change -> Owner: platform-eng (Priya to link PR).
- Design: collaborator pool for prototype -> Owner: Evan.

Action items (next 5 days):
- [Maya] Draft front-end acceptance spec + basic wireframe screens (due 2026-02-19).
- [Priya] Implement two templated intake rules in a feature branch and demo (due 2026-02-20).
- [Evan] Build Figma click-through for Model Variant Rollouts (initial draft due 2026-02-24).
- [Liam] Open infra ticket for per-route p95 availability and list constraints (due 2026-02-16).
- [All] Quick sync on Mon 2026-02-16 10:00 for final cut into Sprint 28.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep UI copy light — avoid 'SLO' jargon for first pass. Use 'Latency budget' language.
- If telemetry is hard, fall back to a 'soft' mode that only raises console alerts.
- Save implementation complexity for post-MVP (e.g., enforcement + throttling later).

Linked tickets / refs:
- JIRA-1024 (Route budgets epic), JIRA-1102 (Intake rules), GH PR https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/548 (intake rule prototype).

Version history / decisions:
- 2026-02-12: initial stitchboard created by Maya.
- 2026-02-15: workshop votes collected; ROUTE-BUDGETS selected as primary.
- 2026-02-17: added acceptance criteria and action owners; pushed to in_review.

If you disagree with the scope call it out inline — this doc is intentionally permissive and meant for rapid feedback.

---
